transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Time: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Mira Chen, Ethan Park, Sofia Patel, Liam O'Connor, Noah Brooks, Isabella Reyes, all-hands attendees (remote)

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto-generated): Leadership gave updates on ARR growth, product roadmap focused on Dedicated & Private, discussed an outage on 8/29 and mitigation plan, shared hiring and org changes, then opened to Q&A.

[00:00] Mira: Hey everyone, good morning good afternoon — welcome to the September all-hands. I know some folks are traveling, appreciate you joining. Quick housekeeping: slides will be posted after the meeting and we'll keep Q&A to the end but drop questions in chat.

[00:20] Mira: Quick win shoutouts before we jump in? Sofia, you want to kick off?

[00:28] Sofia: Yeah thanks Mira. Two quick wins: Dedicated latency improvements on the new kernel shipped to staging last week, we're seeing ~15% p50 improvement on 2k sequence workloads, which is great. Also PS shipped the first set of quantized model profiles that reduce cost per token for some customers by ~20%.

[00:50] Crowd: applause, claps (audio)

[01:10] Ethan: Adding to that, infra did a lot of kernel tuning plus better KV cache management; there's still more to do around warm-up at scale but the numbers look encouraging.

[01:35] Mira: Awesome. Business update — Noah?

[01:40] Noah: Sure. High level: ARR is up 35% year-over-year, usage growth accelerated in Aug largely driven by churned customers moving to Dedicated and a couple of new enterprise pilots. Pipeline is strong; we have 3 deals > $500k in late stages. That said, our expansion motions are a bit slower in EU due to some regs asks — we're addressing that with the Private offering work.

[02:20] Mira: Good. Now the harder item — incident recap. Liam, take us through 8/29 outage.

[02:30] Liam: Yep. On 8/29 we had a cascading failure in the autoscale controller when a new kernel roll hit a specific model shape. The autoscaler mis-estimated memory pressure leading to OOMs on a subset of nodes; that caused degraded throughput and increased latencies for about 45 minutes during peak. Root cause is a mismatch in the kernel memory model + a race in KV cache cleanup.

[03:10] Liam: Immediate mitigation: we rolled back the kernel, scaled up a warm standby pool, and disabled the new autoscale heuristic. Longer term: fix the kernel mem accounting, add a safety breaker to autoscaler, and expand our chaos tests to cover this scenario.

[03:40] Mira: Thanks. Important question — any customer data exposure?

[03:47] Liam: No data exfiltration. Logs show errors but no access pattern outside normal. We still will run external audit for SOC evidence and include it in the postmortem.

[04:05] Mira: Good. Action items on this: Liam to publish the postmortem and timeline, Ethan to lead infra fixes, Sofia to update status for customers.

[04:25] Ethan: Quick technical note — the KV cache race repros in staging if you compress the sequence buffer and then force a partial evict; it's subtle, took us a bit to hit. We're adding guarded free lists and an instrumentation flag to trace memory accounting.

[05:00] Employee question (chat): What does this mean for SLAs?

[05:05] Mira: We're not changing our SLA baseline but we're pushing on better SLOs for Dedicated customers and longer retention for logs in Private. We'll also add a reliability SLA add-on for critical tiers.

[05:30] Isabella: On hiring — we closed recruiting for full-stack infra engineers and we're ramping interviews for 4 senior infra roles and 3 product managers. Offer acceptance has improved since the new comp bands but we still need to close more SRE hires.

[06:05] Mira: Good. Any org changes?

[06:10] Isabella: No major org shuffles; small adjustments in Platform to centralize rollout and observability. Also adding a new manager for Developer Experience in October.

[06:30] Sofia: Product roadmap high level: next 45 days focus on Dedicated perf, Private onboarding flow, and Optimize features for intelligent batching and quantization recommendations. We'll also ship API-level structured output improvements and better function-calling ergonomics.

[07:00] Sofia: For Dedicated specifically: we plan a canary next week to validate the autoscale safety breaker, and a larger rollout in mid-October with new perf targets documented in Console. The Dedicated team is also working on burst capacity gating for sudden spikes.

[07:30] Mira: Any updates on Private / on-prem?

[07:35] Sofia: Private is being trialed by 3 customers now; onboarding flow needs streamlining. We're working on a simplified installer and improved KMS integration. Also, auditing and logging improvements for compliance (SOC2/ISO) are on the roadmap.

[08:05] Audience: brief murmur (some folks typing)

[08:20] Noah: Sales update — pilots: one large fintech pilot is testing Private with strict residency reqs, and a healthcare prospect is running Dedicated with our optimize recommendations. We expect a decision on both before the end of Q4.

[08:40] Employee question (live): Are we planning layoffs or hiring freeze?

[08:45] Mira: No layoffs planned. We are being deliberate about hiring — prioritize revenue-driving and reliability roles. Compensation review is happening mid-September.

[09:05] Employee question (chat): Will we open more regions?

[09:10] Ethan: Yes, roadmap includes EU central and APAC region expansions, but timing depends on partner capacity and Dedicated demand. Private can be used for sensitive regional needs in the interim.

[09:30] Q&A opens — mixed questions on roadmap, SLAs, and R&D timelines.

[10:00] Audience Q: Any plans to open-source parts of the runtime?

[10:10] Ethan: We like the idea but it's a balancing act — some infra libs could be open-sourced to help community benchmarking, but core serving optimizations and operator are strategic. We'll explore releasing tooling and evaluation harnesses.

[10:40] Audience Q: How are we measuring customer satisfaction?

[10:45] Noah: We're doing NPS surveys at pilot milestones, plus monthly health checks for Dedicated customers. We're also tracking latency SLO breaches and quality regressions via our eval suite.

[11:10] Sofia: A quick product note — Optimize now surfaces model+quantization recommendations per route in Console, and we've got a beta for automated batching suggestions based on observed seq length distributions. Expect more UX polish soon.

[11:40] Liam: Follow-up on incident: we're adding more synthetic traffic tests at peak concurrencies and a canary harness that runs KV cache churn scenarios before kernel rollouts.

[12:05] Employee question: Will we offer a lower-cost hosted tier?

[12:10] Mira: We're exploring a community/entry tier that uses heavier quantization and higher batching to reduce costs, but it's not immediate. Product will evaluate with growth.

[12:35] Quick shoutouts: Engineering ship team, PS customer success on recent pilots, and People for new onboarding improvements.

[12:55] Mira: Recap of action items — publish incident postmortem, update roadmap deck, process for pilot invites, hiring priorities updated. Thanks everyone. We'll post materials and the recording.

[13:10] End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: speaker attribution partially auto-generated; some names may be abbreviated or generic. Occasional mis-hearings: 'KV cash' instead of KV cache, 'BPC' for VPC in a couple places.
